Notebook introduction

This document provides an exhaustive, mathematically rigorous, and structural technical manual for the **Spatial Deformation, Composable Vector Field, Generic Custom Functions, Continuous Texture Projection, and Homotopy Animation Subsystem** in the Retiam WebGPU Engine.
1. Mathematical Foundations & Design Motivation
In computer graphics and mathematical animation (such as 3Blue1Brown's Manim), spatial transformations fall into two categories:

items: **Affine Transforms (Linear)**: Represented by $4 \times 4$ matrices ($\mathbf{M} \mathbf{p}$), supporting only translation, rotation, scale, and shear. Straight lines strictly remain straight lines.

**Non-Linear Spatial Deformations (Non-Affine / Non-Euclidean)**: Represented by continuous vector fields $\mathbf{F}: \mathbb{R}^3 \to \mathbb{R}^3$ or complex analytic mappings $f(z): \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$. In these transformations, straight lines, coordinate grids, and textures curve, twist, ripple, or compress.

B. Conformal Mappings
A complex function $f(z) = u(x, y) + i v(x, y)$ is **conformal** if it is holomorphic ($\frac{\partial f}{\partial \bar{z}} = 0$) and satisfies the **Cauchy-Riemann equations**:

blocks.tex: \frac{\partial u}{\partial x} = \frac{\partial v}{\partial y}, \quad \frac{\partial u}{\partial y} = -\frac{\partial v}{\partial x}

blocks.text: Conformal transformations preserve local angles and infinitesimal shapes, making them foundational for fluid dynamics, electromagnetism, and complex analysis visualizations.

blocks.text: C. Generic & Custom User-Defined Fields
You are never restricted to built-in presets. Any mathematical function can be used as a vector field:
1. Plain Anonymous Callbacks
2. Custom Complex Analytic Maps (Field.conformal)
3. Stateful / Physics-Driven Classes implementing ISpatialField
4. Layer 2: Universal Subdivision Engine (src/engine/utils/SubdivisionEngine.ts)

Because GPU vector lines and polygon boundaries are defined by discrete vertices, applying a non-linear function to a straight line with only 2 vertices ($P_0, P_1$) would only move the endpoints without bending the middle.
A. Metric-Driven & Tolerance Options (SubdivisionOptions)
When `maxSegmentLength` or `accuracy` is specified, `SubdivisionEngine` computes dynamic steps per segment based on spatial distance:
This ensures long lines receive ample vertices to curve smoothly, while short segments avoid wasteful vertex allocations.
B. Linear Polyline & Polygon Subdivision
C. Packed 3D Float32Array Zero-Allocation Subdivision
Subdivides tightly packed `[x, y, z, 0]` vertex buffers directly for GPU pipeline consumption:

blocks.code: SubdivisionEngine.subdividePackedVertices3D(data: Float32Array, vertexCount: number, options?: number | SubdivisionOptions): Float32Array;

blocks.text: D. Analytical de Casteljau Bézier Curve Subdivision

For quadratic ($P_0, P_1, P_2$) and cubic ($P_0, P_1, P_2, P_3$) Bézier curves, linear subdivision introduces chord error. `SubdivisionEngine` implements exact **de Casteljau recursive curve splitting**:

blocks.code:
SubdivisionEngine.splitCubicBezier(p0, p1, p2, p3, t): [[Vec2, Vec2, Vec2, Vec2], [Vec2, Vec2, Vec2, Vec2]];
SubdivisionEngine.subdivideCubicBezier(p0, p1, p2, p3, depth): [Vec2, Vec2, Vec2, Vec2][];

7. Concrete Entity Implementations
A. NumberPlane ([NumberPlane.ts](../src/engine/entities/composites/coordinates/NumberPlane.ts))
Deformable coordinate system with horizontal/vertical grid lines, metric accuracy controls, and coordinate conversion helpers:

items: **`maxSegmentLength` & `accuracy`**: Configures segment density for grid lines.
**`c2p(x, y)`**: Converts mathematical coordinate units to world space units $\mathbb{R}^2 \to \mathbb{R}^3$.
**`p2c(p)`**: Converts world space position back to coordinate space.

blocks.text: B. MeshSprite ([MeshSprite.ts](../src/engine/entities/composites/geometry/MeshSprite.ts))
Continuous textured triangle mesh grid ($M \times N$ vertices, $2(M-1)(N-1)$ triangles) with **fixed or custom Vec3 UV coordinates** $(u, v) \in [0, 1]^2$.

items: **1:1 Coordinate Pinning**: Every pixel is mathematically locked to coordinate position $(x, y)$. When the field $\mathbf{F}(x, y)$ bends space, the image features stretch and warp in exact synchronization with the `NumberPlane` iso-curves.
**Zero GC Allocation**: Mutates vertex positions in-place on the WebGPU buffer at full **120 FPS**.

children: Raw WebGPU textures (`GPUTexture`) and `SubTexture` atlas regions.

blocks.text: C. PixelGrid ([PixelGrid.ts](../src/engine/entities/composites/geometry/PixelGrid.ts))
Deformable matrix of 2D polygon tiles for pixel art, heatmaps, and discrete lattice simulations.
D. Path, SVG, Line3D, Poly

items: Packed WebGPU vertex buffers updated directly via `Float32Array`.
In-place vertex warping avoiding CPU Earcut re-triangulation.
